gaps.text: Combining several spectroscopy methods (data fusion) (NIR and Raman would be measured through one combined probe so that both spectra come from the same small area of the powder, since data from different methods must be collected from the same spot. The two streams are then normalised to a common time step, and the concatenated variables are scaled so that neither method dominates the model. Each method keeps its own calibration and diagnostics, and the fused model must beat the best single method on held-out runs, otherwise the extra instrument is dropped.)
No supplied source gives a detection limit, accuracy or response time for API concentration measured in a tablet-press feed frame.
No supplied source states a probe design, window material, pressure or temperature rating for a feed-frame installation.
Laboratory checks are a valid reference for whether the blend is on target.

items.finding: The study explored low-level data fusion by concatenating preprocessed NIR and Raman spectra and mid-level data fusion using extracted features.
items.how_it_applies: This is directly relevant to the planned concatenation of NIR and Raman streams; the pilot could compare low- and mid-level fusion against the best single method on held-out runs.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: Abstract only; the study used a specific platform formulation and API ranges, and it does not detail time alignment, scaling, or the held-out run strategy.

citation.quote: For model development and validation, low-level data fusion was explored through concatenation of preprocessed NIR and Raman spectra. Mid-level data fusion was also evaluated, based on extracted features of the preprocessed data.
citation.label: E04 ¶1

items.finding: The review states that before fusing data from multiple sources, it is essential to evaluate the contribution of each dataset to the model and its complementarity.
items.how_it_applies: This supports keeping each method's own calibration and diagnostics and only retaining the extra instrument if the fused model beats the best single method on held-out runs.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: A general PAT review, not a feed-frame or tablet study; it gives no specific fusion algorithm, scaling method, or acceptance threshold.

citation.quote: Before fusing data from multiple sources, it is essential to evaluate the contribution of each dataset to the model and its complementarity.
citation.label: E02 ¶82

items.finding: The study found that obtaining the same sample size took considerably longer in the feed chute than in the feed frame, and because of segregation and mixing, the feed frame was preferred for in-line blend potency monitoring.
items.how_it_applies: This suggests the feed-frame position may reduce the time needed to collect a comparable sample, but it does not provide a detection limit, accuracy or response time; the pilot should measure time-to-sample and sample size.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: Abstract only; specific tablet press, formulations and NIR setup; no numeric response time, detection limit or accuracy is given.

citation.quote: Because of the considerably longer measurement time needed to obtain the same sample size inside the feed chute compared to the feed frame, the possibility of powder segregation inside the feed chute and the additional powder mixing inside the feed frame, the latter is preferred over the feed chute for in-line blend potency monitoring.
citation.label: E05 ¶1

items.finding: The study found paddle speed and turret speed were the only compression parameters affecting lead-lag, and lead-lag decreased with increasing paddle speed for the first formulation.
items.how_it_applies: This suggests the pilot should control and record paddle and turret speed because they can affect the timing between in-line NIR and off-line tablet measurements; no numeric response time is given.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: Abstract only; a specific tablet press and formulation; the effect direction may differ for other blends, so transfer is uncertain.

citation.quote: Paddle speed and turret speed were the only compression parameters affecting lead-lag. Lead-lag decreased with increasing paddle speed for the first formulation.
citation.label: E05 ¶1

items.finding: The study used a single NIRaman Combi Fiber Probe to combine NIR and Raman for in-line blend potency determination in a rotary tablet press feed frame.
items.how_it_applies: This shows a combined NIR/Raman fiber probe has been used in a feed frame, so the pilot could ask vendors about a similar probe; however, the abstract gives no window material, pressure or temperature rating.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: Abstract only; no probe design details, materials, installation dimensions or environmental ratings are reported; the formulation and press are specific.

citation.quote: This study investigated the added value of combining both near-infrared (NIR) and Raman spectroscopy into a single NIRaman Combi Fiber Probe for in-line blend potency determination in the feed frame of a rotary tablet press.
citation.label: E04 ¶1

items.finding: The study defines lead-lag as the difference in time and API concentration between the in-line NIR response in the feed frame filling chamber and the off-line NIR tablet response.
items.how_it_applies: This warns that an off-line tablet check may not be a same-time reference for the blend in the feed frame; the pilot should account for lead-lag when comparing lab results with in-line measurements.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: Abstract only; specific formulations, tablet press and NIR setup; lead-lag was affected by paddle and turret speed, so transfer to other processes is uncertain.

citation.quote: Lead-lag is defined as the difference in time and API concentration between the measured in-line NIR response inside the filling chamber of the feed frame and the off-line NIR tablet response.
citation.label: E05 ¶1

items.finding: The study found that the in-line NIR response in the dosing chamber closely followed the tablet NIR response.
items.how_it_applies: This supports using off-line tablet measurements as a reference, but only for the dosing chamber and with the study's timing; the pilot should verify this relationship on held-out runs.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: Abstract only; 'closely following' is not exact agreement, and the result is for specific formulations, a specific press and NIR setup; no lab reference method details are given.

citation.quote: The in-line NIR response inside the dosing chamber of the feed frame was found to be closely following the tablet NIR response.
citation.label: E05 ¶1
